course_title: Clinical and Dermatoscopic Diagnosis in Skin Cancer Practice
course_description:
This course addresses clinical recognition and detailed dermatoscopic assessment of skin lesions seen in primary care and dedicated skin cancer practices. This includes a focus on benign, pre-malignant and malignant keratinocytic tumours, naevi and melanoma.

IMED7002 builds on the knowledge from IMED7001, expanding dermatoscopic expertise beyond basic decision-making algorithms. The course delves deeper into "Chaos and Clues" and "Prediction Without Pigment" through an in-depth study of Revised Pattern Analysis, popularised by Harald Kittler. This approach goes beyond deciding whether to excise, observe, or leave a lesion alone, aiming to establish a firm differential diagnosis before biopsy.

Learning is facilitated through reading material, weekly one-hour Zoom tutorials, online clinical cases, and weekly quizzes.

You are required to have access to clinical cases for part of the assessment process

restrictions: Restricted to students enrolled in the GCMed (Skin Cancer), MMed (Skin Cancer), or Non-Award applicants who satisfy the admission requirements for the GCMed (Skin Cancer)

course_contacts.name: Medical School Student and Academic Administration Team

timetable:
Additional timetable information
Each week, specific topics are covered, and you are expected to keep up with the course. Weekly assessments will contribute to your final overall mark. Monday evenings, there will be an online tutorial via Zoom. Towards the end of the semester, visiting dermatopathologists will join these meetings to discuss the histological features of lesions. While attendance at the Zoom meetings is not compulsory, it is strongly encouraged. If work or other commitments prevent you from attending on Monday evenings, efforts will be made to record the meetings for later viewing, although technical issues may sometimes affect the recordings.
course_aims: To equip you with the skills to confidently make provisional and differential diagnoses of lesions encountered in primary care and skin cancer practice, based on clinical and dermatoscopic examination, and to appreciate the dermatoscopic histopathological correlation of same.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply clinical and dermatoscopic principles and lesion recognition techniques in diagnosing skin cancer.
Analyse and evaluate dermatoscopic patterns to inform diagnostic pathways and refine clinical reasoning.
Demonstrate awareness of public health issues and collaborative practice in skin cancer prevention.
Integrate cultural and social awareness in dermatoscopic assessments, particularly for underserved communities.
Present and explain dermatoscopic findings clearly and accurately to peers and patients.
Model ethical, accurate documentation and decision-making in dermatoscopic practice.

assessment_details.title: Individual Student Case Assignments
assessment_details.task_description: You will produce a portfolio of 5 (five) cases of skin lesions (benign and malignant melanocytic, benign and malignant keratinocytic, inflammatory, adnexal, other malignant, vascular, infiltrates, etc). Each case will require a positional, clinical close-up (macro) and dermatoscopic photo of the lesion, a provisional and differential diagnosis and a copy of the histopathology report (where applicable). Then, a short list including incidence, clinical features (typical size and distribution, shape, border, colour, surface features), dermatoscopic features (pattern, colours, and clues), and any associations. This information will need to cite the limited references used to compile the information. The portfolio will be due by the end of Week 10. Inadequate or suboptimal photos and/or poor dermatoscopic assessment result in a mark of less than 7/10. The overall mark for the portfolio will constitute 20% of the final grade. Weekly Zoom Meeting An online tutorial meeting via Zoom. The meeting will be hosted by the course co-ordinator and lecturers and will at times include a guest lecturer. The meeting schedule will be posted on Learn.UQ . This will be a forum for discussing the previous week's material and new clinical cases. The focus is to refine your dermatoscopic assessment of skin lesions. It is planned that these meetings will be recorded for the benefit of those who may be unable to join the meeting in real time.
